label: Self-released
description: Charlie Hill (formerly recording as Chazzy Lake) writes plainspoken indie country songs anchored by pedal steel and a warm, conversational drawl. Chuck Pond moves between wistful road songs and blunt breakup lines without ever raising its voice much above a murmur. It's for listeners who want the twang of Nashville's DIY scene without the polish of Music Row.
lineage: Grows out of the Nashville indie-country underground alongside labelmates like Jana Horn and Hand Habits; feeds the same audience as the wider Twangy Indie Folk scene.

label: Earth Libraries
description: Charlie Reed is a Chicago band, not a solo artist, built around delicate, subdued folk-rock that swells with strings and pedal steel. Eddy is an intimate debut about cyclical thinking and getting stuck, drawing on Karen Dalton's phrasing (a live cover of hers is a setlist staple) filtered through hushed indie-folk arrangements.
lineage: Part of the Chicago DIY folk circuit that overlaps with Whitney and Dehd's Earth Libraries labelmates; feeds the same Twangy Indie Folk audience as Charlie Hill and Lou Turner.

label: Mtn Laurel Recording Co.
description: Carmen Perry, best known as the voice of power-pop punks Remember Sports, steps into vivid, conversational solo songwriting on her debut. Eyes Like a Mirror trades her band's crunch for earthy, understated arrangements and a subtle twang, with lyrics that read like diary entries turned into short stories.
lineage: A songwriter's turn toward twang from the 2010s DIY punk scene, following a path similar to labelmate Lou Turner and Mtn Laurel's other cosmic-country-adjacent signees.

label: Dead Oceans
description: Cassandra Jenkins writes wry, spoken-sung character studies set to warm, unhurried arrangements of guitar, sax and synth. My Light, My Destroyer follows her breakout An Overview on Phenomenal Nature with more of the same searching, half-narrated songwriting, colorful without ever raising its voice.
lineage: Extends the Drag City deadpan school's narrated-song tradition into 2020s indie folk, name-checked alongside Cassandra's own generation of New York songwriters.

album: Well Once There Was A King
label: Historic NJ Recordings
description: A sprawling, 24-song grab-bag from an Oregon home-recording project, Well Once There Was A King cycles through folk, slacker jangle, country, doom-metal detours and Beach Boys harmonies without pausing for breath. It rewards the same magpie curiosity that draws people to Guided by Voices' overstuffed records.
lineage: Descends from the lo-fi, kitchen-sink home-taping tradition of GBV and Sebadoh, filtered through a 2020s Bandcamp DIY sensibility.

label: Fat Possum
description: A stark breakup record built from voice, piano and pedal steel, Old Flowers is Courtney Marie Andrews at her most unadorned, with a Ronstadt-range voice carrying every ounce of the heartbreak. It's the record that crossed her from journeyman Americana singer to a defining voice of the 2010s-20s twangy-folk revival.
lineage: Bridges 1970s Laurel Canyon songwriting (Ronstadt, Mitchell) into the modern indie-folk scene; her later records lean further into full-band cosmic country.

label: Fat Possum
description: Loose Future opens Courtney Marie Andrews back up into full-band, '70s-Nashville-flavored arrangements after the bare-bones Old Flowers, with buttery lead guitar and warm harmonies replacing the earlier record's silence.
lineage: A direct continuation of the country-rock/Cosmic American Music lineage, following her own path from stripped-down folk into the cosmic country revival.
key_tracks: These Are the Good Old Days

label: Mama Bird Recording Co.
description: Dean Johnson sings timeless, uncluttered cowboy waltzes in a soulful tenor that recalls classic countrypolitan records more than any indie trend. Nothing for Me, Please is spare and patient, letting his voice and the pedal steel do the emotional work.
lineage: Sits in the singer-songwriter lineage of 1970s country balladeers, adopted by the 2020s indie-folk scene via Mama Bird's Pacific Northwest roster.

label: St. Itch
description: Ellie O'Neill's debut sets calm, alto-led vocals against austere, minimalist arrangements that occasionally bloom into ornate pastoral rock. Touchstones like Laura Marling and Joni Mitchell are audible, but Time of Fallow's Irish folk grounding and biblical imagery give it its own hushed gravity.
lineage: Draws on British/Irish folk-rock songwriting (Fairport Convention, Sandy Denny) reframed through the 2020s international indie-folk scene.

label: Keeled Scales
description: An Ohio farm girl turned Nashville songwriter, Emily Hines builds her debut around efficient, lived-in folk-rock arrangements: acoustic and electric guitar, cello, and a voice that shifts easily between plainspoken and soaring. These Days is unfussy small-town storytelling delivered with real conviction.
lineage: Fits the Keeled Scales roster's twangy-folk lineage alongside labelmates Tenci and Buck Meek, feeding off the same Townes-to-Gillian-Welch folk line as the rest of the label.

label: Fire Talk Records
description: Fran is the project of Maria Jacobson, whose stunning, unadorned voice carries Leaving's songs of grief and climate anxiety. The record sits at a crossroads of loss and possibility, its melodic guitar and string arrangements never overpowering the plainspoken lyrics.
lineage: Part of the Fire Talk Records roster's hushed, homespun indie-folk wing, alongside labelmates like lots of hands.

label: Patchwork Label
description: Gawshock makes quiet, homespun Southern indie folk out of Huntsville, Alabama, the kind of unhurried songwriting that favors atmosphere and repetition over hooks. Leaves to the Sun continues the lo-fi thread of the project's earlier self-titled record and Unless If EP.
lineage: A small-town Southern branch of the Bandcamp DIY folk network, feeding the same audience as other regional home-recording projects covered by No Expectations.

label: Self-released
description: Recorded in a West Toronto garage, Georgia Harmer's debut spans intimate folk and strummy country into sophisticated jazz-pop, unified by her poised, wise-beyond-her-years songwriting about friendship and fleeting moments. It comes from a family of Canadian artists and poets and sounds like it.
lineage: Part of the Canadian singer-songwriter continuum running from Gordon Lightfoot-adjacent folk through the 2020s Bandcamp indie-folk scene.

label: Mtn Laurel Recording Co.
description: Hannah Pruzinsky's second album, co-produced by Florist/Told Slant's Felix Walworth, threads Wurlitzer, saxophone and synth through an explorative, quiet folk framework. Red sky at morning is a meditation on love, control and domesticity that never raises above a gentle murmur.
lineage: Grows directly out of the Florist/Told Slant hushed-folk orbit that also feeds Modern Slowcore's C8 lane.

label: Luminelle Recordings
description: Helena Deland's second album pairs graceful, evocative songwriting with delicate acoustic arrangements and glittering Sam Evian production. It's smart, literary indie folk more than straight twang, but its acoustic-led intimacy places it alongside the wider 2020s Bandcamp folk revival.
lineage: A Montreal singer-songwriter lineage that runs parallel to Ada Lea and other Canadian indie-folk artists of the same scene.
borderline_note: Included on Terry's coverage; her songwriting leans more indie-pop/folk than twangy, a judgment call to include over exclude.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
description: Kayla Cohen's fifth album as Itasca pairs patient, exploratory fingerstyle guitar with feathery vocals and a dreamlike sense of immersion. It's the vocal-song counterpart to her American Primitive-indebted instrumental work, produced with Robbie Cody.
lineage: Bridges the American Primitive solo-guitar tradition (V8) into song form, feeding the same Twangy Indie Folk audience as Marisa Anderson and William Tyler.

label: Tender Loving Empire Records
description: New Zealand-raised, Los Angeles-based Jess Cornelius (formerly of Teeth & Tongue) sings arresting songs about personal upheaval with striking lucidity and emotional nimbleness. Co-produced by Mikal Cronin, CARE/TAKING is her sophomore solo album after years fronting an Australian indie-rock band.
lineage: Moves from the Flying Nun/Antipodean indie tradition of her earlier band toward the plainspoken American singer-songwriter scene.

label: Self-released
description: kitship's am i a rock? is eight low-key songs of acoustic singer-songwriter fare and understated lo-fi indie rock, built on commanding vocals and instant, unfussy melodies. A guest spot from Sharp Pins ties it into Chicago's current DIY guitar-pop scene.
lineage: Part of the current Chicago Bandcamp slacker/lo-fi network that also includes Sharp Pins.

label: Self-released
description: Recorded solo in three days, This Is Music strips conversational songwriting down to a pristine, understated croon over sparse guitar and piano. It's a bedroom-scale record that trades ambition for intimacy.
lineage: A solo bedroom-folk record in the same DIY tradition as other Bandcamp-only singer-songwriters covered by No Expectations.

label: Saddle Creek
description: Ada Lea's third album is her most playful and breezy, a slice-of-life record steeped in '70s Laurel Canyon folk with wry humor and Dylan nods baked into the song titles. It's a lighter turn from Alexandra Levy after two more anxious, indie-rock-leaning records.
lineage: A Montreal songwriter's turn toward Cosmic American Music, following the same 1970s country-rock revival line as Kacey Johansing and Cass McCombs.

label: Gar Hole Records
description: Raised in Appalachian Pennsylvania and nicknamed "The Rose of Appalachia" for her clawhammer banjo playing, Angela Autumn folds American folk and bluegrass roots into a hybridized, arena-sized sound on Believer, blending indie, psychedelia and gothic country.
lineage: Grows out of Appalachian old-time and bluegrass tradition, recast through the 2020s cosmic-country revival's bigger, more psychedelic production.

label: YK Records
description: Annie Williams's debut is a refreshing, tasteful set of subtle pop melodies and conversational, funny writing, arranged sparsely by a crew of Nashville session players. Visitor favors wit and understatement over big hooks.
lineage: Part of the current Nashville indie-folk underground built around small labels like YK Records.

label: Mtn Laurel Recording Co.
description: A member of the band TOLEDO, Aïda Mekonnen Caby steps out with pristine, dreamy folk-pop dressed in the same big-indie production polish as her main band, but at a more intimate, personal scale on Mais Uma.
lineage: Feeds off the TOLEDO/Winspear-adjacent Brooklyn indie-pop scene while drawing on folk songwriting fundamentals.

label: Tiny Engines
description: Recorded to tape in three days at a farmhouse above Venice, Allora is a chaotic, ecstatic record of hymnlike tenderness and full-band catharsis, made by Ben Seretan and his touring band mere weeks after the death of a close friend. It swings between grief and communal joy without settling on either.
lineage: Ben Seretan's prolific solo catalog (a 24-hour drone record, weekly song series) sits at the DIY, home-recording end of the indie-folk network.

label: Self-released
description: Albany's Blue Ranger thrives in a muted palette of rustic, anxious folk, its slow-unfolding arrangements and violin textures building patiently toward small eureka moments rather than choruses.
lineage: Upstate New York's DIY folk network, adjacent to other regional home-recording acts covered by No Expectations.

label: Western Vinyl
description: Ian Hatcher-Williams's Lamplight debut is pastoral folk rock made modern by Kevin Copeland's (Lightning Bug) deft production, intricate but immediate, with hooks as strong as anything on Coldplay's Parachutes. Songs move between love, panic attacks and quiet self-forgiveness.
lineage: Connects Brooklyn's Lightning Bug-adjacent indie-folk scene to the wider Western Vinyl roster's ambient-folk lineage.

label: Dear Life Records
description: A former field scientist who spent years surveying National Park visitors, Lindsay Reamer turned those observations into a debut full-length that finds humor rubbing shoulders with heartbreak, acoustic guitars brushing against synthesizers, in a folk-rock-pop matrix indebted to Sheryl Crow.
lineage: Grew out of the Philadelphia DIY folk-rock scene, following her Dear Life Records EP Lucky.

label: Thirty Tigers
description: Lizzie No plays harp and sings charming, infectious Americana that closes out cosmic-country showcases with ease. Halfsies, her third album, is a genre-defying concept record released jointly through Thirty Tigers and her own imprint, Miss Freedomland.
lineage: A Black singer-songwriter carving her own path through the cosmic-country and new-outlaw scenes built on Gram Parsons' and Emmylou Harris's country-rock lineage.

label: SPINSTER
description: Lou Turner's third solo album is a spacious, intimate cycle of cosmic country songs recorded live in an Alabama barn with Nashville's Styrofoam Winos. Her warm voice and nylon-string guitar carry domestic-scale observations in a lineage she traces explicitly to Silver Jews, Lambchop and Bill Callahan.
lineage: Directly cites the Drag City deadpan school (Silver Jews, Bill Callahan) and 1970s singer-songwriters (Joni Mitchell, Michael Hurley) as touchstones.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: Led by Chicago musician Chet Zenor, Lucky Cloud crafts dreamy, jazz-tinged indie rock full of rich textures: pedal steel, soft grooves and unorthodox melodies. Foreground is the project's debut full-length after growing from a solo bedroom project into a full band.
lineage: Part of the same Chicago Ruination Record Co. roster as Sima Cunningham, feeding into the city's twangy indie-folk scene.

label: Acrophase Records
description: Mali Velasquez writes folk-inflected indie rock that swings between hushed verses and explosive choruses, a fresh voice landing somewhere between Katy Kirby and Indigo De Souza. I'm Green is her full-length debut.
lineage: Part of the same Nashville-adjacent folk-indie wave as Katy Kirby, drawing on the Townes-to-Gillian-Welch folk line filtered through 2020s bedroom-pop dynamics.

album: Before You Turn Into a Dog
label: Self-released
description: Andy Weaver (drummer for Widowspeak, Castanets and his own band Wildflower) records intimate, handmade songs at home under the name Ruby of Thanks. Before You Turn Into a Dog values process over polish, preserving first-take performances of songs about love, work and finding peace.
lineage: Sits squarely in the Woodsist-orbit lo-fi home-recording tradition (Little Wings, John Andrews and the Yawns, Hand Habits), which itself descends from the DIY home-taping network.

label: Self-released
description: Hunter Park's project She Returns From War bills itself as "Cosmic Americana from South Carolina," and Ruthless leans into dance-pop elements alongside its country roots, cheekily needling Nashville conventions along the way.
lineage: A Southern songwriter reworking cosmic-country tropes with modern pop production, part of the same Southeastern DIY circuit as Minor Moon and V.V. Lightbody collaborators.

label: We Be Friends Records
description: Sheepskin, the Burlington duo of Molly Meehan and Sam Tiesworth, trade tasteful dual vocals over gentle, unhurried arrangements that recall the Canvasback/Asthmatic Kitty era without slipping into twee. Pirate Ship Playground is quietly sung and carefully built.
lineage: Part of the tight-knit Burlington, Vermont scene alongside Vega and Charlie Hill's Vermont collaborators.

label: Self-released
description: Written and recorded at home by Meredith and friends, Neighbors is a set of mismatched feelings about moving: what you keep, what you leave behind, how you hold onto family when everyone scatters. It's plain, homemade indie folk, unpolished by design.
lineage: A home-recording project in the same DIY vein as other Bandcamp bedroom-folk acts covered by No Expectations.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: One half of the duo Finom (formerly Ohmme), Sima Cunningham steps out solo on High Roller, an ornate but emotionally heavy folk record cut with Clay Frankel that closes on a cathartic grief song for a friend.
lineage: Extends the Chicago DIY folk-rock scene that runs through Finom and the wider Ruination Record Co. roster.

album: A Swollen River, A Well Overflowing
label: Keeled Scales
description: Fronted by Jess Shoman, Tenci's second album pairs quiet, wandering folk arrangements (guitar and saxophone) with Shoman's distinctive quavering voice. It's tender, hushed songwriting that never quite resolves its unease.
lineage: Part of the Keeled Scales roster alongside Emily Hines and Buck Meek, feeding the modern hushed-twang lane out of the Chicago DIY scene.
key_tracks: A Swollen River, A Well Overflowing

label: Antiquated Future Records
description: Adrian O'Barr's Wildflower project makes leafy, vibrant folk with ample twang and jazz-minded experimentation, featuring members of Destroyer, Cut Worms, Widowspeak and the Huntress and Holder of Hands. Green World is a coastal-Maine song cycle about noticing the quiet.
lineage: Connects Maine's DIY folk scene to the wider indie-folk/Woodsist-adjacent network through its guest musicians.

label: Triangle House / Sophomore Lounge
description: Will Lawrence's fifth album mines a dusky, nostalgic, tasteful palette across eight understated folk-rock songs. Rooftops in the Centerfold is masterful in its restraint, favoring mood over showmanship.
lineage: Part of the Sophomore Lounge/Triangle House roster's rural indie-folk lineage, which overlaps with the Woodsist-adjacent scene.

label: Polyvinyl
description: Ella O'Connor Williams's debut as Squirrel Flower is a hushed, unsettled record about drowning and being pulled under, quiet indie folk-rock that occasionally breaks into noise. It set the template for her louder, twangier records to come.
lineage: An early, quieter entry in an evolving catalog that grows steadily louder and more countrygaze-indebted with each release.

label: Polyvinyl
description: Tomorrow's Fire pushes Squirrel Flower toward dense, hooky guitar walls over programmed drums, a louder and more countrygaze-adjacent record than her earlier hushed work. Tracks like "Intheskatepark" are propulsive, feedback-laced and anthemic.
lineage: Marks Squirrel Flower's move toward the countrygaze/loud-twang sound that defines C4, following the template Wednesday popularized.

label: Drag City
description: The Australian duo of Helen Franzmann (Baby Alpaca) and Mick Turner (Dirty Three), Mess Esque write flat, wry, literary songs on their third record, named in reference to Franzmann's late sister Jay Marie. It's spare, deadpan songwriting squarely in their label's house style.
lineage: A direct extension of the Drag City deadpan school (Silver Jews, Bill Callahan) via an Australian branch of the same label roster.
key_tracks: Take Me To Your Infinite Garden
borderline_note: This is a V-zone (Drag City deadpan school) act rather than Core; included here per assignment's C8 Terry sweep with the best-fit lane set to V2.

label: Last Gang Records
description: Loving, the Victoria, BC band of sophisticated songwriters, work at a deliberate, unhurried pace on their second album Any Light, an existentially uncertain but mysteriously optimistic record built on patient arrangements.
lineage: A Pacific Northwest-adjacent quiet-rock band whose slow tempos and hushed dynamics connect to the slowcore lineage more than straight twang.
borderline_note: Not strongly twangy; included per assignment's C8 Terry sweep on the strength of its slow, hushed dynamics.

label: New Martian Records
description: Maine-born, Queens-based, The Clearwater Swimmers' self-titled debut flips between hushed intimacy and full electric-guitar surges, drawing direct comparisons to Neil Young's Harvest Moon and Jason Molina's Magnolia Electric Co.
lineage: Sits squarely in the Neil Young/Crazy Horse and Molina/Magnolia Electric Co. lineage that defines indie twang.

label: Self-released
description: A Fort Wayne trio's debut, Marketplace is sparse but pretty slow-burn indie rock, understated in a way that hints at more to come from the band.
lineage: A small-city Midwest slowcore act working in the quiet-dynamics tradition that runs from Duster and Bedhead through today's hushed-twang scene.

label: Self-released
description: Dead Sullivan is the lo-fi, indie-rock solo project of multi-instrumentalist Boone Patrello, whose later band Teethe grew directly out of it. Imbecile is a scrappy, homemade record that longtime fans (including Teethe's Will Taylor) still cite as a favorite.
lineage: A direct predecessor to Teethe, part of the same Texas lo-fi/slowcore lineage feeding today's hushed-twang scene.

label: Self-released
description: Fine's debut Rocky Top Ballads is impeccably crafted minimalist songwriting with rootsy, bluegrass-tinged elements and a Hope Sandoval-style hush over every track.
lineage: Part of the current hushed-twang wave that pairs slowcore dynamics with bluegrass instrumentation, in the vein of Duster-descended acts.

label: Self-released
description: Finnish Postcard's debut Body is dynamic, swinging from homespun quiet to raging full-band noise, with natural harmonies and touchpoints that run from Elliott Smith to Pinback to Owen.
lineage: Part of the lo-fi/slacker DIY network that runs from Elephant 6-style home recording through today's bedroom-pop-adjacent indie rock.

label: Fire Talk Records
description: into a pretty room is winsome, ramshackle bedroom folk built from flickering electronics and processed vocals, aimed at fans of Hovvdy, Pinback and Alex G.
lineage: Part of the Fire Talk Records hushed-bedroom-folk roster alongside Fran, feeding the modern slowcore lane's DIY, home-recording wing.
